problems.statement: The forced move from downtown Castellan Hall (2,150 seats, by the rail station) to the remote, smaller Brightwater venue (1,290 seats, poor late-night transit) caused the step-drop in attendance, especially among single-ticket buyers and low-attendance subscribers.
The music director's shift toward post-1945 works and commissions is the main driver of the ticket revenue decline.

A sector-wide secular decline (ageing subscribers, cost of living, post-2020 habits) is a material contributor; comparable orgs with no venue change lost a similar 25-35% over the same period, so the venue effect cannot be assumed to be the whole 30%.
Invisible or ineffective marketing, attributed to the music director, is driving the decline.

Marketing effectiveness generally (agency, mix, a vacancy June-Sept 2024) may be a weak contributor, but it cannot be assessed because no attribution tracking exists and spend and open rates look normal.
Two price increases (about +16% average price) contributed to lost buyers independently of the venue move.

The board's evidence base is weak: the presented case rests on a self-selected correspondence file, a press column with no per-concert data, and the chair's framing, while the organization lacks marketing attribution and separation of venue from other effects.

Non-renewing the music director carries a concrete financial downside (Halvorsen key-person clause, about $400k per season, plus risk to the $180k State Arts Council grant tied to commissions) while addressing a cause the evidence does not support.

causalClaims.from: Castellan Hall closure / move to Brightwater (distance, transit, parking, fewer seats)
causalClaims.to: Step decline in single-ticket sales and subscriber attendance and renewal in 2023-24
Growth of low-attendance subscriber households that fail to renew

causalClaims.from: Patron complaint emails and press column
causalClaims.to: Repertoire as the cause of the decline

actions.action: Do not base a non-renewal vote on the ticket-revenue decline; renew or offer a short extension before the 31 Dec 2026 notice deadline, and assess the director separately on artistic and leadership criteria.
actions.rationale: The decline is not attributable to her programming (E7, E8, E12, E5), and non-renewal would forfeit about $400k per season in Halvorsen funds and endanger the commissions-linked grant (E15).

actions.action: Accept the cathedral's six offered 2026-27 dates and put the highest-demand programs downtown at St. Aldric.
actions.rationale: Cathedral concerts sold about 48% more tickets with about $31k higher contribution each, and attract single-ticket buyers, regardless of programming (E11).

actions.action: Fix Brightwater access: late shuttle or extended bus service synced to a 22:15 finish, parking subsidy or bundles, and safety communications.
actions.rationale: Travel, parking and safety were the largest named reasons for lapse and reduced attendance (E12, E8, E9), and the hall will not return until at least Sept 2027.

actions.action: Run a targeted win-back campaign to lapsed patrons and low-attendance subscriber households, anchored to downtown dates and transport help.
actions.rationale: 71% of lapsed respondents said they would likely return (E12) and the 0-2 attendance group renews at only about 44% (E5).

actions.action: Instrument marketing with campaign/channel attribution and keep price and channel tests small and controlled.
actions.rationale: Marketing's contribution is currently unmeasurable (E14, E16) and the board cannot judge it without data.

actions.action: Build the 2026-28 budget and grant plans on the assumption that Brightwater lasts through 2027-28 and that secular softness continues.
actions.rationale: The Castellan reopening has already slipped to Sept 2027 (E9) and peers still show declines of about 12% a year (E10).

actions.action: Retreat from new works or commissions to win back audience.
actions.rationale: Within-venue sales show no penalty for post-1945 works (E7), the survey ties only 11-12% of attrition to programming (E8, E12), and the State Arts grant requires two commissions per season (E15).

actions.action: Blame or replace the marketing team or agency now.
actions.rationale: Spend is flat and engagement metrics look normal, but without attribution there is no evidence of marketing failure (E16, E14).
Price effects are confounded with the venue change and peers raised prices about 14% as well (E14, E10, E12).

actions.action: Issue a non-renewal notice and start a director search because of the revenue decline.
actions.rationale: It targets a cause the evidence rejects, risks key-person grant losses, and leaves the venue and access problem untouched (E15, E7, E12).

nextEvidence: Decompose the decline using pre-move trend (2019-22) and peer ticket volumes/prices, plus patron geography (postcode/distance) before and after the move, to size the venue effect versus the secular trend.
Controlled comparison of cathedral and Brightwater programs matched on repertoire and date, extended over the 2026-27 cathedral dates, to confirm the location effect and any programming effect.
Marketing attribution (campaign, channel, source codes) and price-sensitivity data to test marketing and pricing as contributors.
output.summary: The evidence does not support the chair's account. Ticket revenue fell as a step in 2023-24, when the orchestra moved from downtown Castellan Hall to Brightwater, which has 40% fewer seats, a 6.5 km distance and poor late-night transit, then stayed roughly flat. Within Brightwater, concerts with major post-1945 works sold as well as others, engaged subscribers' renewal held at about 85%, and lapsed patrons cite travel far more than programming. Peers lost a similar share without moving, so secular decline also contributes. Marketing reports to the Executive Director, not the music director, and cannot be assessed. Do not non-renew on revenue grounds; it risks about $400k a year in grants. Use cathedral dates and access fixes, and add attribution tracking.
